rv.q: This is all funny stuff, but it can't make up for the fact that, once established, the political throughline never becomes integral to the book.

After dwelling with such craven procrastination on the fine ingredients that make up "The Frogs," I am forced to concede that what should have been a zesty, airy souffl� is a soggy, lumpy batter that never shows the slightest signs of rising.
The new pieces are sweet and funny, but marrying them to the older seventies-era numbers makes for an erratic score.
The current version of The Frogs is a rather different beast from what, by all reports, was seen at Yale long ago.
But the vehicle carrying these messages is so shaky that they're delivered time and time again with minimal impact.

cn.t: Despite Nathan Lane's crowd-pleasing performance, this Sondheim-Aristophanes update struggles with its ambitious political satire, leaving critics divided on whether the blue-ribbon talent can salvage an unfocused and overly earnest production.

vs.sum: The Vivian Beaumont Theater offers exceptional sightlines and sound quality due to its unique thrust stage design, ensuring a great view and auditory experience from nearly every seat. While the ambiance is enhanced by its location within the Lincoln Center, the comfort level is average with some reports of tight seating, and facilities are typical for a Broadway venue.

acc.note: Orchestra accessible via elevator. Induction hearing loop for t-coil. Loge NOT accessible (stairs only).
